Direction, Made Visible

"When the compass agrees with the room, the room finally feels like it belongs to you."

Our Approach

Vastu that supports modern living — not one that creates fear of it.

Every consultation starts the same way: we walk the space, note how light enters, where the family actually sleeps, cooks and gathers, and where the structure already works in its favour.

Only then do we suggest anything — and almost always, the fix is smaller than people expect. A shifted mirror, a repositioned desk, a colour changed in one room. Major structural work is the exception, not the starting point.

Every idea we bring is explained in plain language: which direction it concerns, which element it balances, and why it should help — no jargon left unexplained, no instruction taken on faith.

Vastu in Practice

What a well-aligned space actually looks like.

Real corners of real homes — entrance, prayer space, foyer and living areas — shaped around the same principles behind every consultation.

Main Entrance

The Approach

The main entrance is the first thing Vastu evaluates — its direction sets how energy enters the household. A shaded, lit pathway with living greenery on either side is treated as a good sign, easing the transition from outside to in.

Prayer Corner

The Ishaan Corner

Traditionally placed in the north-east — the Ishaan corner — a prayer space is kept the cleanest, quietest part of the home. Fresh flowers, a lit diya and an uncluttered floor matter just as much as the idol itself.

Foyer Alignment

First Impression

The foyer is the first indoor space energy reaches after the entrance, so its layout gets read carefully. A mirror is angled away from directly facing the front door, and a console with a soft rug helps ground the space.

Water & Greenery

Elements at Work

This corridor brings two elements together directly — Jal (water) through the small fountain, and Prithvi (earth) through the planted shelves. Along a north or east wall, moving water like this is meant to keep energy circulating rather than sitting still.

Prosperity Wall

A Statement Anchor

A tree motif on this scale is often read as a Kalpavriksha, the wish-fulfilling tree of abundance. Anchoring a reception or living wall, it's typically positioned toward the north — the direction Vastu associates with wealth and opportunity.

Living Spaces

Shared Comfort

Living rooms do best in the north, east or north-east, where a household naturally gathers in daylight. Here the seating opens toward the entrance, the television sits in the south-east fire corner, and layered lighting keeps the room from feeling clinical.

How a Consultation Runs

Four visits' worth of thinking, in one clear sequence.

Step 1

Site visit

We walk the property in person, measuring orientation and noting how each room is actually used.

Step 2

Direction mapping

Compass readings are taken at the plot and matched against the room layout.

Step 3

Recommendations

A written, explained set of corrections — ranked from simplest to most involved.

Step 4

Follow-up

We check back after changes are made, and adjust if something isn't settling right.
